simple: one of the jobs a chip's pin can be switched to.
analogy: a doorway that can be the way to the kitchen or the way to the bar, but not both at once.
precise: a peripheral signal (UART transmit, SPI clock, timer channel) that a pin can be routed to by the GPIO configuration; the possible functions of each pin are listed in the MCU's datasheet, and a pin carries one function at a time.
source: D6 of F10-29 (The datasheet (alternate-function table), reference manual (DMA request mapping, flash organisation, vector table offset) of the microcontroller on the course's flight controller) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a text file that says what every pin of a flight controller's chip is used for and which sensors are on the board.
analogy: the floor plan of a new restaurant.
precise: a per-board configuration file read at build time by a generator script, which checks it against the microcontroller's tables and produces headers and linker settings for the HAL backend; ArduPilot documents such "hwdef" files for its ChibiOS boards.
source: D2 of F10-29 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a number that says which board a firmware file was built for.
analogy: the restaurant's name on the floor plan.
precise: an identifier compiled into both the bootloader and the application image; the bootloader and the upload tools compare them so that firmware for one board is not flashed onto another.
source: D2 of F10-29 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a small program at the start of the chip's flash that can load new firmware over USB.
analogy: the restaurant's back door, through which the new floor plan is delivered.
precise: a separate image in the first flash sector(s) that runs after reset, waits briefly for an upload over USB or serial, checks the image, and then jumps to the application at a fixed offset.
source: D2 of F10-29 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a small operating system for microcontrollers that many flight controllers run under ArduPilot.
analogy: Nadia's reflexes, which decide in a split second which job gets her attention first.
precise: an open-source embedded software project made of a real-time kernel (ChibiOS/RT, threads with fixed priorities and kernel objects) and a hardware abstraction layer (ChibiOS/HAL, device drivers with a common model), joined by an operating-system abstraction layer; ArduPilot's porting documentation describes new boards as STM32-based boards running ChibiOS.
source: D1 of F10-27 (ChibiOS project, "ChibiOS documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a second, bigger computer on the drone that does heavy jobs, like vision, and talks to the flight controller.
analogy: the assistant walking beside the waiter.
precise: a Linux-class computer on the vehicle connected to a flight controller serial port (or network), running programs that exchange MAVLink with the autopilot as a separate component of the same system, for example to send position targets in a guided mode.
source: D2 of F10-31 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a secret-looking extra byte, computed from a message's definition, that is mixed into its checksum.
analogy: each code card has a watermark; a message checked against the wrong card fails.
precise: a byte derived from the message's name and its fields' types and names; sender and receiver mix it into the frame checksum, so a frame whose definition differs between the two sides is rejected instead of misread.
source: D3 of F10-30 (MAVLink project (Dronecode Foundation), "MAVLink Developer Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the file the flight controller writes during a flight, with everything it measured and decided.
analogy: the waiter's diary.
precise: a binary log written by the autopilot to onboard storage (an SD card or flash chip), containing records from sensors, estimator, controllers, modes, events and parameters at their own rates; ArduPilot calls these DataFlash logs for historical reasons.
source: D2 of F10-32 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one particular list of message types that two programs agree on.
analogy: the code card printed for one restaurant.
precise: an XML definition file (which may include others) listing enums and messages with IDs and fields; MAVLink has a common set and additional dialects maintained by flight-stack projects. Both ends must be generated from compatible definitions.
source: D3 of F10-30 (MAVLink project (Dronecode Foundation), "MAVLink Developer Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: deciding which peripheral gets which DMA helper.
analogy: sharing out a few trolleys between many jobs.
precise: the assignment of streams to peripheral requests at build time, under the constraint that each request may use only its listed streams; when streams run out, some requests run without DMA or share a stream.
source: D2 of F10-29 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a helper in the chip that moves data between a peripheral and memory without the processor.
analogy: a trolley that carries glasses between bar and tables while the waiter does other things.
precise: one of a fixed number of DMA engine channels; each peripheral request can be served only by certain streams (a table in the reference manual), and a stream serves one request at a time unless the software shares it.
source: D6 of F10-29 (The datasheet (alternate-function table), reference manual (DMA request mapping, flash organisation, vector table offset) of the microcontroller on the course's flight controller) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the rule that a driver must be switched on before you use it, and in which order its functions may be called.
analogy: picking up the tray before walking, putting it down before letting go.
precise: the documented set of states of a HAL driver object (for example uninitialised, stopped, ready, active) and the calls allowed in each; ChibiOS/HAL drivers are started with a configuration structure and stopped to release the peripheral, and calls in the wrong state are caught by checks in debug builds.
source: D1 of F10-27 (ChibiOS project, "ChibiOS documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a list of facts from the log, in time order, that explains what happened.
analogy: "the lights flickered, then Kofi lost sight of the tables, then he stopped".
precise: a time-ordered sequence of logged observations, each linked to the next by a known mechanism (a parameter, a failsafe rule, a control law), ending in the observed outcome, with competing explanations checked against the same data.
source: R5 of F10-32 (lab runs of dfread.py and analyse.py on the synthetic glitch log, this build); the five-step forensic method of the University Authoring Guide

simple: the work the flight controller does every single loop, before anything else.
analogy: keeping the tray level at every step.
precise: the time-critical path run once per main-loop period: read the inertial sensors, update attitude estimation, run the rate and attitude controllers and send motor outputs; other work is scheduled around it.
source: D2 of F10-28 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one way of flying, such as "hold position" or "come home", written as its own piece of code.
analogy: different ways of walking: carrying, clearing tables, standing by the bar.
precise: a class derived from a common mode base, with functions to enter the mode (which may refuse), run it every loop and report what it needs (for example a position estimate); the vehicle switches modes through one call that records the reason.
source: D2 of F10-28 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one entry of the legend.
analogy: "line starting with T means: time, table, glasses".
precise: a record of a reserved type that defines another record type: its numeric type, total length, short name, one format letter per field, and comma-separated field labels; the FMT record also describes itself.
source: D2 of F10-32 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one message as bytes on the wire, with a beginning marker and a check at the end.
analogy: one complete radio call: "who, to whom, what, over".
precise: a start byte, a header (length, flags, sequence number, system ID, component ID, message ID), the payload, and a 16-bit checksum; MAVLink 2 adds optional signature bytes.
source: D3 of F10-30 (MAVLink project (Dronecode Foundation), "MAVLink Developer Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the program on a laptop, tablet or phone that shows where the drone is and lets a person plan and command a flight.
analogy: the head waiter's desk.
precise: a MAVLink endpoint, usually with system ID reserved for ground stations, that displays telemetry, uploads missions and parameters, and sends commands over a telemetry radio, USB or a network link.
source: D2 of F10-31 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a flight mode in which the drone flies wherever another computer tells it, one target at a time.
analogy: the assistant saying "table 6 now".
precise: a mode in which the autopilot accepts position, velocity or attitude targets over MAVLink from a ground station or companion computer, while keeping its own stabilisation and safety checks.
source: D2 of F10-31 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a set of "plugs" through which the main program uses hardware, without knowing which chip is behind them.
analogy: Nadia's way of carrying, which works on every floor.
precise: a software layer that defines interfaces (serial ports, timers, buses, storage, scheduling) and hides each platform's implementation behind them; the word names two different layers in this chapter: ChibiOS/HAL (drivers for one microcontroller family) and ArduPilot's HAL (interfaces that the vehicle code uses, implemented once per platform).
source: D1 of F10-27 (ChibiOS project, "ChibiOS documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the part that makes the plugs work on one kind of computer.
analogy: learning one hall's floor.
precise: a concrete implementation of every HAL interface for one platform; ArduPilot documents backends for ChibiOS boards, for Linux boards and for SITL on a desktop computer.
source: D2 of F10-27 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a short message each system sends regularly to say "I am here, and this is my state".
analogy: each waiter clicking the walkie-talkie once a second.
precise: a periodic message announcing the sender's type, flight stack, mode and status; receivers use heartbeats to discover systems and to detect a lost link.
source: D3 of F10-30 (MAVLink project (Dronecode Foundation), "MAVLink Developer Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a piece of ArduPilot that every vehicle can use, such as the IMU code or the logger.
analogy: skills every waiter has, whatever the restaurant.
precise: a directory of C++ classes for one function (a sensor family, the estimator, attitude control, motors, navigation, missions, logging, parameters, the MAVLink link, the scheduler), shared by all vehicles and reaching hardware only through the HAL.
source: D2 of F10-28 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: what the drone does on its own when it stops hearing from whoever is directing it.
analogy: go back to the meeting point.
precise: a rule in the autopilot that, when no heartbeat has arrived from the controlling ground station (or companion) for a configured time while it matters, switches to a configured action such as return, land or continue.
source: D2 of F10-31 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the message language drones, ground stations and companion computers use to talk to each other.
analogy: the walkie-talkie code words of the waiters.
precise: a lightweight, binary, message-based protocol in which each message type is defined in an XML file and code for packing and parsing is generated from it; the MAVLink Developer Guide describes two wire versions, MAVLink 1 and MAVLink 2.
source: D3 of F10-30 (MAVLink project (Dronecode Foundation), "MAVLink Developer Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: passing messages between several links so that each reaches the program it is meant for.
analogy: the waiter relaying a message from the kitchen to the head waiter.
precise: a node with several links learns on which link each system and component was heard, forwards broadcast messages to all other links and targeted messages only to the link of their target.
source: D3 of F10-31 (MAVLink project (Dronecode Foundation), "MAVLink Developer Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a small conversation made of several messages, used for one job, such as uploading a mission.
analogy: the fixed sequence of calls to take an order: "table 4 ready" — "go ahead" — "two still" — "copy".
precise: a protocol on top of messages with defined roles, sequences, timeouts and retries; the MAVLink guide documents microservices such as heartbeat and connection, mission, parameter and command protocols.
source: D3 of F10-30 (MAVLink project (Dronecode Foundation), "MAVLink Developer Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a thin adapter that lets the driver code run on top of a kernel.
analogy: the few words of a hall's language that Nadia needs to ask for a door to be opened.
precise: the interface through which ChibiOS/HAL drivers use kernel services (locking, waiting, waking a thread from an interrupt), so that the HAL can be used with ChibiOS/RT or with another kernel.
source: D1 of F10-27 (ChibiOS project, "ChibiOS documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a named setting stored on the flight controller, such as a gain or a failsafe action.
analogy: the restaurant's house rules, written on a card.
precise: a named, typed value with a default, kept in the board's persistent storage and exposed to ground stations over MAVLink; ArduPilot organises parameters in groups that belong to libraries and vehicle objects.
source: D2 of F10-28 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the list of jobs the flight controller does now and then, each with how often and how long it may take.
analogy: Kofi's list of other jobs.
precise: a static table of entries (function, desired rate in hertz, declared maximum run time, and in recent releases a priority) that the scheduler walks after the fast loop, running each due task whose budget fits into the time left in the period.
source: D2 of F10-28 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a log file that contains its own explanation of how to read it.
analogy: the legend at the front of the diary.
precise: a format in which special format records declare, for every record type, its name, length, field types and field names; a reader decodes the rest of the file from those declarations without a built-in message list.
source: D2 of F10-32 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how a sensor chip is turned on the board compared with the board's forward direction.
analogy: a sign on the plan saying "this table faces the window".
precise: a fixed rotation applied in software to a sensor's axes so that its readings are expressed in the board frame; a wrong rotation makes the estimator see rolls as pitches or the wrong sign.
source: D2 of F10-29 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: running the real flight software on a computer, flying a simulated vehicle.
analogy: practising the evening's walk in an empty hall with pretend trays.
precise: a build of the flight stack for a desktop HAL backend whose sensors and actuators are connected to a physics simulator, so that the same vehicle code can be tested without hardware; ArduPilot documents its SITL and the simulators it can connect to.
source: D2 of F10-28 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a strip of memory below a stack that nobody should ever write.
analogy: a "do not step here" strip at the edge of the stage.
precise: memory placed beyond the end of a stack and painted or protected (by a memory protection unit where one exists), so that an overflow is detected instead of silently corrupting a neighbour.
source: D1 of F10-27 (ChibiOS project, "ChibiOS documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: filling a thread's stack with a known pattern before it runs, then counting how much of the pattern was overwritten.
analogy: chalk lines on the floor that show how far the waiter ever walked.
precise: a measurement of the maximum stack depth a thread has written, obtained by filling its stack area with a fill value at creation and scanning from the far end for the first overwritten word; it can be fooled when a frame reaches past the end of the stack, because writes that land outside the painted area are not seen (Layer 3).
source: D1 of F10-27 (ChibiOS project, "ChibiOS documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: two numbers saying which vehicle (or ground station) sent a message and which part of it.
analogy: "this is restaurant 1, waiter Kofi".
precise: the system ID identifies a vehicle or ground station on the network; the component ID identifies a part of that system (the autopilot, a camera, a companion computer); targeted messages carry a target system and target component in their payload.
source: D3 of F10-30 (MAVLink project (Dronecode Foundation), "MAVLink Developer Guide") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the longest time a job promises to take.
analogy: "this will take me at most ten seconds".
precise: the per-task time in the table that the scheduler compares with the time remaining before starting the task; it is a promise made by the developer, not enforced by preemption, so a task that exceeds it delays everything after it.
source: D2 of F10-28 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a recording, made by the ground station, of the messages it received over the radio.
analogy: the head waiter's notes of what Kofi said on the radio.
precise: a timestamped capture of the MAVLink stream at the ground station; it holds only what was sent at telemetry rates and received, while the onboard log holds what the autopilot recorded at its own rates, including during link loss.
source: D2 of F10-32 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the part of ArduPilot that makes one kind of vehicle behave like that vehicle: a multirotor, a plane, a rover or a submarine.
analogy: the habits of a waiter in one particular restaurant.
precise: a top-level program per vehicle type that owns the main loop, the task table, the flight modes and the failsafe logic, and uses the shared libraries through their interfaces; the ArduPilot documentation lists Copter, Plane, Rover and Sub among the vehicles built from one source tree.
source: D2 of F10-28 (ArduPilot project, "ArduPilot documentation") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
